content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of forecast horizon).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then sharply decline, suggesting overshoot after spikes.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias — forecasts often revert to historical mean too quickly, missing sustained trends.
- Forecasts are overly sensitive to recent spikes; model reacts too aggressively to short-term volatility.
- Model underestimates downward trends after major price spikes; fails to recognize momentum reversal.
- Forecasts for later days (e.g., 20–30 days) show diminishing accuracy, suggesting horizon-specific decay in predictive power.
- Model tends to overcorrect downward movements, leading to premature bottoming out.
- Forecasts often lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, especially in downward trends.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher prices in the 30-day forecast, even when historical mean is lower.
